scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

I'm 33 years old and have been living with my parents most of my life. They charge me $200, which seems reasonable given where we live. Recently, there was a toilet flood in my bathroom, so they had to remodel my section of the house. Because of this, we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to lock myself in my room most of the time to avoid them, but now that's not possible. Today, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to get up and help bring in the groceries. I told her I'd do it in a minute. I was too into the game to notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I told him I'd do it in a minute. He said, "A minute is now," grabbed the controller out of my hand, and it turned into a huge shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which is basically impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They have their golden child, of course, but to throw his success in my face is bullshit. I mean, I guess I could have gotten up and helped them, but to me, because I pay rent, that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation? I'm not sure. On one hand, I pay rent, so I think I have some right to set boundaries. On the other hand, living with parents usually comes with some expectations of contributing to the household, even if it's just helping out with small things like bringing in groceries. Maybe I should consider why they were so upset. They had to remodel my section of the house because of the flood, which probably disrupted their routine and made it harder for them to avoid me. Then, when they came back from Costco, I was too engrossed in my game to help out, which might have made them feel like I'm not contributing my fair share. I also think about how I used to lock myself in my room to avoid them, which might have made them feel neglected or unappreciated. Now that the remodel is happening, we're interacting more, and it's causing tension. Another thing to consider is the comparison to my younger brother. They're using his success to make me feel bad, which isn't fair. But maybe they're feeling stressed or frustrated with the situation, and they took it out on me. I also wonder about the practicality of them expecting me to find a place to live by Friday. That's a short time frame, and finding a new place can be really stressful, especially if I'm not prepared for it. Overall, I think there's some fault on both sides. I should have been more considerate of their needs and helped out with the groceries, even if I pay rent. They, in turn, should have communicated their feelings more calmly instead of grabbing the controller and causing a shouting match. Maybe the best approach is to talk things out calmly, apologize for not helping, and try to find a middle ground where I can contribute more to the household while still maintaining my independence. It's important to respect each other's boundaries and work together to make the living situation better for everyone.
